explanation: Beckoning with a single curled index finger (the Western 'come here' gesture) is generally less common in India and much of Asia; a more typical polite way to call someone over is an open hand, palm facing down, with the fingers scratching inward together. No strong India-specific evidence was found that single-finger beckoning is a severe insult there the way it is in some neighboring cultures, but it can still come across as abrupt or commanding rather than respectful.
local_tip: To call someone over, extend your hand with the palm facing down and bring your fingers in together, rather than curling a single finger toward yourself.

also_check.note: The polite beckoning form uses a palm facing the recipient at head height; reversing it is considered impolite.
Beckoning with a curled finger is considered highly offensive and has historically been associated with calling animals.
Less taboo than in parts of Asia, but curling a single finger to beckon can still feel abrupt; an open-hand wave is more neutral.
